candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment → Management of Care, printed p. 7 (PDF pageno 10): provide/receive handoff, collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, assess referral needs, implement provider orders, initiate/evaluate/update the plan of care and utilize resources to promote quality care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Handoff, referrals, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continuity of care
candidate.educational_objective: Coordinate complex discharge care by reconciling multidisciplinary recommendations, clarifying orders and referrals, updating the plan of care, and providing an accurate handoff so the client has a coherent follow-up plan.

options.A: Reconcile the plan with the multidisciplinary team, clarify unresolved orders or referrals, update the care plan and discharge information, and ensure an accurate handoff so the client knows the next steps.
options.B: Give the client each discipline's separate instructions without clarification because coordination between services is outside the nurse's role.
options.C: Cancel specialty follow-up and direct the client to use only one provider so conflicting recommendations cannot occur.
options.D: Limit care coordination to insurance authorization and leave clinical referrals, handoff, and plan-of-care discrepancies unresolved.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places multidisciplinary collaboration, handoff, referral assessment, implementation of provider orders, updating the plan of care, advocacy, and use of resources to promote quality care within Management of Care. AASLD also describes advanced/decompensated cirrhosis as a condition with multidisciplinary physical, psychosocial, nutritional, and palliative-care needs, reinforcing the importance of coordinated care across services. B is incorrect because the nurse has an explicit Management-of-Care role in collaboration and continuity and should not knowingly pass unresolved discrepancies to the client. C is incorrect because eliminating indicated specialty services is not an appropriate method of resolving conflicting instructions. D is too narrow: administrative authorization may be one component of coordination, but it does not replace clinical reconciliation, referrals, handoff, or care-plan management. The final item tests an observable nursing coordination decision rather than memorization of a generic case-manager job description.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current NCSBN test plan directly supports multidisciplinary collaboration, handoff, referral coordination, provider-order verification, care-plan updating and resource use as Management-of-Care nursing activities; current AASLD guidance independently supports the multidisciplinary nature of advanced cirrhosis care.

candidate.stem: A client with advanced liver disease is preparing for discharge. The hepatology, nutrition, and social-work plans contain different follow-up instructions, and the client is unsure which appointments and referrals are required. Which action by the nurse best supports continuity of care?
